name: Hepatocyte (liver cell)
blurb: The main cell of the liver: a many-sided cell packed with mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum, lying in a one-cell-thick plate beside blood channels, with a bile channel grooved into the wall it shares with its neighbours.
note: Model: a human hepatocyte, cut in half. Measured in human liver: the number of cells per gram of liver and the share of the liver they make up, from which its volume is worked out; that some cells have two nuclei and that at least a quarter are polyploid. Illustrative: the shape and its sides, the shares of the cell taken by the nucleus and the organelles (textbook figures whose species is not stated), the size and count of every organelle drawn, the widths of the bile canaliculus, microvilli and blood channel, the amount of glycogen, and the colours. The neighbouring cells are drawn faintly.

volume.calc: 80% of the liver is hepatocyte (openstax_liver) of 1 cm³ (taking 1 g of liver as 1 cm³, an assumption) = 0.8 x 10^12 µm³, divided by 1.07 x 10^8 cells per gram (wilson2003): 7,477 µm³; the range uses 0.65 and 1.85 x 10^8 cells per gram
volume.compare: a cube of 15 µm edge is 3,375 µm³ (lodish_cube); rat mononucleate hepatocytes 4,800 to 6,000 µm³ (hepcell)
volume.note: illustrative estimate worked out from two measured numbers and one assumed density; the cell count is a yield from isolation (all cells, living and dead, counted in suspensions of isolated liver cells from seven livers), not a count of hepatocytes in intact liver; another estimate, 1.2 x 10^8 hepatocytes per gram (Hirota 2001, quoted in PMC5341582), gives about 6,700 µm³

width.note: illustrative: a six-sided cell this wide and 17 µm tall has about the worked-out volume

volume_fraction.note: a textbook share for a liver cell (alberts_table); the species is not stated, so it is shown as illustrative for the human

nucleus.note: Some human hepatocytes have two nuclei, and at least 25% of adult human hepatocytes are polyploid (polyploid_review); no source opened gives the share with two nuclei. One nucleus is drawn, with a pale (euchromatic) look as in the liver micrographs; the position and the nucleolus are illustrative.

volume_fraction.note: textbook share of a liver cell (alberts_table), species not stated; shown as illustrative

mitochondria.size_note: illustrative: each about 1.0 µm³, so 22% of 7,500 µm³ gives about 1,650, in line with about 1,665 per cell measured in rat liver (Weibel 1969; human count not found); real liver mitochondria vary from small spheres to elongated rods

count.calc: illustrative, not checked against any count: 1% of a 7,500 µm³ cell (alberts_table, species not stated) in lysosomes of 0.4 µm, each 0.034 µm³

illustrative, not checked against any count (one histology atlas gives about 200 to 300 peroxisomes per hepatocyte): 1% of a 7,500 µm³ cell (alberts_table, species not stated) in peroxisomes of 0.5 µm, each 0.065 µm³

count.note: illustrative: droplets are seen in liver micrographs (columbia_em); how many a cell holds depends on diet

stacks.note: illustrative; about 1% of the cell volume (alberts_table)

not_drawn: smooth endoplasmic reticulum (about 5% of the cell)

special.note: Two faces of the cell touch the blood channels (sinusoids) beside the plate, and carry microvilli that reach into the space between the cell and the channel's wall. Where two neighbours meet, a groove in each wall forms a bile channel (canaliculus), sealed from the rest of the gap by tight junctions (columbia_em). These are described, not drawn.
The cells lie in branching plates, often one cell thick, between sinusoids; blood runs toward the central vein and bile the other way (openstax_liver).
illustrative sizes: microvilli about 0.5 µm long and 0.1 µm wide, the blood channel 10 µm wide
grooves in the walls shared with neighbours form the bile channel (openstax_liver); its 1 µm width is illustrative
rough ER about 9% of the cell (alberts_table); the number and size of the stacks drawn are illustrative
illustrative: the amount of glycogen varies with meals

cut: The cell is cut in half: a round, pale nucleus with a nucleolus near the middle, a great many small mitochondria through the cytoplasm, lysosomes and peroxisomes as small dots, a few round lipid droplets, Golgi stacks beside the nucleus, and the faint outlines of neighbouring liver cells behind.

colours.convention: Membrane pale; inside dark; nucleus violet; mitochondria orange; lysosomes, peroxisomes and lipid droplets each a distinct code colour. None of the colours is the real colour of the cell.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.about: The watery inside of the cell, crowded with enzymes. In the liver it holds the stores of glycogen, a branched sugar polymer that is not drawn.

nucleolus.name: Nucleolus
nucleolus.about: The dense region of the nucleus where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosomes begin to be assembled.

lipid_droplet.name: Lipid droplet
lipid_droplet.about: A store of fat (mostly triglyceride, with some cholesterol esters) wrapped in a single layer of phospholipid. Liver cells hold a few, and more after a fatty meal or in a fatty liver.

microvilli.name: Microvilli (face toward the blood)
microvilli.about: Short fingers of membrane on the faces that look onto the blood channels. They reach into the narrow space between the cell and the channel wall and greatly enlarge the surface through which the cell takes up and returns substances. Their size here is illustrative.

sinusoid.name: Blood channel (sinusoid)
sinusoid.about: A wide, leaky capillary of the liver that runs beside the plate of liver cells. Blood from the gut and the liver artery flows through it toward the central vein. Drawn faint, 10 µm wide (illustrative).

canaliculus.name: Bile canaliculus
canaliculus.about: A tiny channel formed by grooves in the walls of two neighbouring liver cells, sealed by tight junctions. The cell secretes bile into it; bile flows the opposite way to the blood, toward the bile ducts. Bile is mostly water (shown), with bile salts, bilirubin and cholesterol. Its width here is illustrative.

rough_er.name: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
rough_er.about: Stacks of flat membrane sacs covered in ribosomes, about 9% of the cell. Here the liver cell makes the proteins of the blood plasma, such as albumin. The ribosomes are shown as one RNA nucleotide, a stand-in.

glycogen.name: Glycogen
glycogen.about: Clumps of glycogen granules, the store of sugar the liver builds after a meal and breaks down between meals to keep the blood sugar steady. Each granule is a branched molecule of thousands of glucose units. The amount drawn is illustrative; it changes with meals.

about: The hepatocyte makes up about 80% of the liver. Its volume, {drawn.cellVolume} µm³ as drawn, is close to 7,500 µm³ worked out from the number of cells isolated per gram of human liver; the real figure varies a good deal from person to person, since the count ranged from 65 to 185 million cells per gram.

The shares of the cell taken by the nucleus (about 6%), mitochondria (about 22%) and the rest come from a textbook table that does not say which species was measured, so they are used here as a guide and marked illustrative. {drawn.mitochondria} of about {drawn.mitochondriaWanted} mitochondria are drawn in this half.

Some liver cells have two nuclei, and at least a quarter of adult cells hold extra sets of chromosomes. One nucleus ({drawn.nuclei} drawn) is shown. The face on the left looks onto a blood channel (sinusoid, drawn faint) and carries short microvilli ({drawn.sideMicrovilli} in this half). Grooves in two of the walls shared with neighbours are the bile canaliculi, into which the cell secretes bile. Stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum ({drawn.erStacks} stacks) make the blood's proteins, and clumps of glycogen store sugar. Their sizes and numbers are illustrative; the smooth endoplasmic reticulum is not drawn.

openstax_liver.cite: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder
openstax_liver.used_for: hepatocytes about 80% of liver volume; bile canaliculi in grooves between cells; sinusoids; blood and bile flow in opposite directions

wilson2003.cite: Wilson ZE et al. (2003) Br J Clin Pharmacol 56:433-440, as listed in BioNumbers entry 110544
wilson2003.used_for: human liver: 1.07 x 10^8 cells per gram (range 0.65 to 1.85 x 10^8), seven livers; the entry page only, the paper itself not read

hepcell.cite: Article PMC5341582 on hepatocellularity and hepatocyte volume in Wistar rats (Tables 1 and 2); it quotes a predicted human value of 120 x 10^6 hepatocytes per gram (Hirota et al. 2001)
hepcell.used_for: rat comparison only: mononucleate hepatocyte 4,789 to 6,044 µm³; binucleate 6,565 to 7,530 µm³; 25 to 34% of rat hepatocytes binucleate

lodish_cube.cite: Wisniewski JR et al. (2014) Mol Cell Proteomics 13:3497, quoting Lodish et al. Molecular Biology of the Cell, 4th ed., as listed in BioNumbers entry 113236
lodish_cube.used_for: hepatocytes described as roughly cubical cells of 15 µm edge (species not given); the entry page only

alberts_table.cite: Alberts B et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, Table 12-1 'Relative volumes occupied by the major intracellular compartments in a liver cell (hepatocyte)', in the publisher's online 7th edition
alberts_table.used_for: cytosol 54%, mitochondria 22%, rough ER 9%, smooth ER 5%, nucleus 6%, Golgi, peroxisomes, lysosomes, endosomes 1% each; the table does not name the species

polyploid_review.cite: Review of diploid and polyploid hepatocytes in liver injury (PMC8056861)
polyploid_review.used_for: at least 25% of adult human hepatocytes are polyploid; a binucleate hepatocyte is always polyploid; it gives no percentage of two-nucleus human cells

leeds_hepatocyte.cite: University of Leeds Histology Guide, Liver: the hepatocyte
leeds_hepatocyte.used_for: branching plates one cell thick between sinusoids; microvilli into the space of Disse; canaliculi are enlargements of the gap between cells; mitochondria, rough and smooth ER and Golgi; smooth ER detoxifies and handles glycogen and bilirubin

columbia_em.cite: Columbia University histology lab 17, electron micrographs of liver
columbia_em.used_for: euchromatic nuclei, abundant mitochondria and ER, lipid droplets and lysosomes; tight junctions seal the canaliculi; microvilli (the canaliculus picture is from rat)
